newsitem.title: GERMANY: German newspapers lose out to magazines-study.
newsitem.headline: German newspapers lose out to magazines-study.

text.p: German newspapers saw a slight fall in the number of readers because of increasing competition from magazines over the last year, an advertising industry study released on Tuesday said.

According to the Allensbach Market and Advertising Media Analysis (AWA 97) by the Institute of Opinion Polling, newspaper readership sank two percent, which the institute said was a result of more magazines appearing on the market.
"The pressure of competition from new titles, above all in the areas of women's and personal computer magazines, has increased further," the institute said in a statement.
The institute said it found that competition in the so-called programme press, or publications which offer cultural or entertainment listings including television guides, continued to intensify.
Three of the top 10 magazines with the highest growth proved were from the programme press.
Nearly 20,000 readers aged over 14 were surveyed in the AWA 97, the institute said.
